newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq slams Britain, Turkey for diplomat visit.
newsitem.headline: Iraq slams Britain, Turkey for diplomat visit.

text.p: An official Iraqi newspaper attacked Britain on Sunday for sending two diplomats into Kurdish-controlled northern Iraq, saying it breached "international norms and conventions".
"What has been done by this 'delegation' represents a flagrant violation of international norms and consular dealings," said al-Thawra, newspaper of the ruling Baath party.

The Kurdish north has been under the control of the Kurds since the 1991 Gulf War following Iraq's invasion of Kuwait. The area is patrolled by U.S. and British warplanes to protect it from Iraqi forces.
In London, a Foreign Office spokesman confirmed two British diplomats from the Ankara embassy visited northern Iraq for a few days last week, as part of a series of "fairly routine" contacts.

The Iraqi government has gained some power in the region since Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) leader Massoud Barzani asked Baghdad to send troops last August to help him fight against the rival patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) led by Jalal Talabani.
The Foreign Office spokesman said the visit was made at the invitation of the PUK and KDP leaderships to assess the situation there.
"We consider given the situation in northern Iraq that such visits are fully justified," he said.
Thawra also condemned Turkey for allowing the diplomats to enter Iraq through its territory.
"We strongly denounce such an act...We consider it immoral and hold the Turkish government responsible...because it allows them to cross the Iraqi-Turkish borders," it said.
The paper urged U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan to "put an end to such incursions and aggressions against Iraq's rights."
